existing_le_goff_edges.relationship: Relates medieval representations and everyday material conditions within a social history attentive to belief and vulnerability.
existing_le_goff_edges.evidence_note: Substantive characterization is attributed to Jean-Claude Schmitt’s account reproduced in the EPHE notice. The existing Purgatory publisher record is supplementary; it does not establish that the monograph was read or that its chronology is uncontested.

existing_le_goff_edges.relationship: Supplies a specifically acknowledged resource on merchant and ecclesiastical temporalities in Thompson’s 1967 time-discipline essay.
existing_le_goff_edges.evidence_note: Primary p. 56 and n. 2 checked afresh: Thompson explicitly identifies Le Goff’s contrast and cites the 1960 and 1963 essays. This records that limited use, not the whole derivation of Thompson’s argument or a universal account of modernization. Le Goff’s cited essays remain unread here.

existing_le_goff_edges.relationship: Ginzburg identifies Le Goff’s specification of cultural interaction as a productive example within his account of popular culture.
existing_le_goff_edges.evidence_note: Preface to the Italian edition, English translation p. xix. This records an explicitly praised methodological example in Ginzburg’s own argument. It does not claim that the cited scholar founded his practice, supplied the entire book’s method or endorsed Ginzburg. John and Anne Tedeschi’s translation and the 1976/1980/1992 distinction remain; the cited scholars’ complete works are not newly read.
